_note: Copy to lsp_servers.json and adapt. Any value in command/args, env, workspaceRoot, initializationOptions or settings may reference an environment variable as ${NAME} (or ${NAME:-fallback}); it is expanded when the file is read, using the process environment including everything in .env. Only the braced form is special, so a bare $ stays literal. An unset name is left as written and reported as a validation note. What is written below is the POSIX form; _windows_note gives the Windows form of the same three entries, and _expansion_note states why one string cannot be both.
_expansion_note: What ${…} does, exactly: each reference is replaced by that one variable's value, or by the text after ':-' when the variable is not set. Several references can sit in one value, a bare $ is literal, and an expanded value is never re-split into separate arguments. What it does NOT do: no conditional, no platform test, no default that depends on the OS. So one template string cannot be correct on both platforms for a PATH — the separator is ';' on Windows and ':' on POSIX, and a ':-fallback' naming the other platform's folders lands in the value verbatim here. That is why the entries below carry the ':'-joined POSIX PATH and the Windows form is a note to copy, not a value. (restricted-paths.txt expands through this same helper, with the opposite rule for a reference that resolves to nothing: there it is dropped and logged rather than kept as written, because an un-expanded prefix would read as a guardrail in force.)
_windows_note: The same three entries in the form verified to start on Windows 11 with a Volta-managed toolchain. Two things differ from below. (1) The PATH separator is ';', not ':'. (2) Write the command as the bare program name — 'pyright-langserver', 'typescript-language-server', 'vue-language-server' — because what npm/Volta install under those names is a #!/bin/bash script Windows cannot exec, and the hub resolves argv[0] with shutil.which over the child's own PATH, which honours PATHEXT and finds the .cmd beside the script. An absolute command works too and is then searched in the folder it spells. Nothing else changes: the workspaceRoots are ${BENCHMARKIT_PATH_LOCATION} for pyright and ${BENCHMARKIT_PATH_LOCATION}/web for typescript and vue. Example entry, Volta in its default location: {"command": ["pyright-langserver", "--stdio"], "workspaceRoot": "${BENCHMARKIT_PATH_LOCATION}", "env": {"PATH": "${LOCALAPPDATA}\\Volta\\bin;${ProgramFiles}\\Volta"}}. That PATH must carry BOTH folders the shim resolves through — the shim folder and ${ProgramFiles}\Volta, where volta.exe and node.exe sit: an env PATH *replaces* the child's PATH wholesale, so naming only the shims starts the shim and fails it with 'volta is not recognized'. The same PATH carries typescript and vue; vue keeps '--tsdk=${BENCHMARKIT_PATH_LOCATION}/web/node_modules/typescript/lib'.

vue.label: Vue
vue._note: Volar delegates TypeScript semantics to its client over the private 'tsserver/request' protocol; core/lsphub (features.py answering via tsserver.py) answers _vue:projectInfo with the workspaceRoot's own tsconfig/jsconfig, which is what unblocks every other request. It does not run a tsserver, so <script> type errors come from the 'typescript' server, not from this one. Needs web/node_modules/typescript and a matching --tsdk.
